[{"cwe_id": "CWE-287", "name": "Improper Authentication"}], "description": "Gitea's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect sign-in flows did not enforce WebAuthn when it was a user's only configured second factor. Users who registered a passkey without TOTP were correctly challenged on password login, but could receive a full authenticated session through OAuth sign-in with no WebAuthn prompt.

Two OAuth-related code paths were affected. One of them could also persist an external identity link during sign-in, extending the impact beyond a single session.

## Affected Versions

All versions up to and including **1.27.0** that support WebAuthn and OAuth2/OpenID sign-in.

## Impact

**Who was affected:** Users who used WebAuthn as their sole second factor (no TOTP enrolled) and signed in through an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider.

**What broke:** WebAuthn is intended to protect accounts when another credential (such as a password or a compromised identity provider session) is known or stolen. On the affected OAuth paths, that protection was not applied. Password-based login continued to enforce the passkey challenge as expected.

| Path | Scenario | Consequence |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Linked-identity OAuth callback | Attacker authenticates with a victim's already-linked external identity | Full session without WebAuthn challenge |
| OAuth account-link sign-in | Attacker links an external identity to a victim account using the victim's password | Full session without WebAuthn challenge; external identity permanently linked to the victim account |

The account-link path was the more serious case: a successful sign-in could bind the attacker's identity provider account to the victim's Gitea account. Subsequent OAuth sign-ins through that provider might no longer require the victim's password, and password rotation alone might not revoke that access.

This issue is separate from [CVE-2026-20779](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-20779), which addressed TOTP replay timing. This advisory concerns which second factors the OAuth sign-in paths considered before granting a session.

## Root Cause

OAuth sign-in handlers determined whether second-factor verification was required by consulting TOTP enrollment only (`GetTwoFactorByUID`). WebAuthn credentials are stored separately and were not checked on those paths before a session was issued.

The password login handler already checked both TOTP and WebAuthn enrollment and redirected to the WebAuthn challenge when appropriate. A combined helper (`HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn`) existed in the codebase but was not used to gate session creation on the affected OAuth handlers.

**Affected components:**

- `routers/web/auth/oauth.go` — linked-identity callback (`handleOAuth2SignIn`)
- `routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go` — account-link sign-in (`oauth2LinkAccount`)
